properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 3 at 11:25AM PST until November 3 at 8:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast beaches.

* WHEN...Through 8 PM Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 3 at 11:25AM PST until November 3 at 8:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, Up to 1.6 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM PST this
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday
to 1 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 8:00 AM
Wednesday 11/4, 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 8:35 AM
Thursday 11/5, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 9:08 AM
Friday 11/6, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 9:38 AM
Saturday 11/7, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06 AM
Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 3 at 10:46AM PST until November 4 at 6:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...West winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...Mojave Desert Slopes.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 6 AM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways impacted include State Routes 14, 58,
and 178, as well as U.S. 395.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.
